text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.
LONDON - Britain's leading blue chip index ended nearly unchanged, near the day's highest level, after an early wave of profit-taking.
The benchmark FTSE 100 index fell 3.2 points to 4,337.8, with decliners outpacing advancers 55 to 41. Turnover was relatively light, capped by Wall Street being closed for a holiday.
FRANKFURT - German shares made gains in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings, erasing losses from the bourse session tied to profit-taking after 11 staight sessions of gains.
The IBIS DAX ended up 11.13 points at 3,260.30 points, with the DAX index ending bourse trade down 15.61 points at 3,232.57.

PARIS - French shares closed higher after having spent most of the day in the red as a stronger dollar in the afternoon provided support in the absence of any Wall Street influence. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 7.06 points or 0.27 percent to 2,634.48.
ZURICH - Swiss shares shrugged off the weaker bias on most European bourses to finish at a second consecutive all-time closing high, boosted by dollar strength and derivatives-linked buying.
The All-share Swiss Performance Index added 26.76 points or 0.94 percent to end at 2,866.19.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed marginally higher, managing to climb for the fifth trading day in a row, but brokers said power to extend gains ebbed in light trading volume as profit-taking pressure was strong below 19,000 on the key market index.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average ended up 28.65 points or 0.15 percent to 18,750.65.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended with modest gains, with a fall in the U.S. long bond yield and gains in the local futures market allowing prices to stabilise after heavy losses last week. The Hang Seng Index rose 31.36 points or 0.24 percent to 13,144.62.

SYDNEY - A confident Australian share market closed higher, helped by investors chasing the yields among the big banks, Commonwealth Bank of Australia was the exception in the bank sector, its stock sliding 53 cents after to A$13.37 after it went ex-dividend 45 cents. The All Ordinaries index added 10.6 points to 2,493.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial stocks rallied to end slightly firmer in futures-related trade and on the back of some late afternoon overseas buying. Gold shares continued positive on a perkier bullion price and brokers said they expected the market to remain firm on Tuesday
The all-share index rose 21.8 points to 7,042.5, industrials ended 10.2 points higher at 8,315.5 and golds gained 23.6 points to 1,418.7.
